summary: Both sides render exact black (all pixels 0,0,0) under every window, dial setting, seed and rig tested, and expose an identical control surface — indistinguishable in every observable respect, but the pattern appears sound-driven and the harness feeds no sensor data, so its real behaviour is unverifiable here.
observations: Original renders without compile or runtime error; port likewise. Neither side is broken in the 'errors out' sense.

Both sides produce exactly zero output at every moment sampled: meanBrightness avg/min/max = 0, motion avg/min/max = 0, zeroMotionFrames = every captured frame, brightnessTrend 'steady' on both, across a 6 s/20 fps baseline, a 60 s/5 fps survey and a 240 s/2 fps extended survey.

This is NOT the dim-pattern false-freeze described in JUDGE.md: a --dump at t=0, 3, 3.05, 10, 20 and 29 s (12-px rig, dial at 0.5) returns literal [0,0,0] for all 12 pixels on both sides at all six times — the zeros are exact, not rounding.
Control surface matches exactly: both sides expose one control, name 'sliderIntegrationTime', kind 'slider', label 'IntegrationTime'. No missing, extra, renamed or re-kinded control.

The survey revealed no regime structure at all — a single uniform all-black regime for the whole 240 s window, with no events, cycles or mode boundaries to park a --skip run inside. A late-window run (--skip 120, dial at 1) is likewise black, so there is no warm-up that eventually fires.
Not seed-dependent (seed 7 identical to seed 1) and not rig-dependent (re-rendered on an 8x8 grid; sheet, motion filmstrip and rhythm images all black on both sides).

The pattern name and the 'IntegrationTime' dial suggest an audio peak-integrator (a sound-reactive envelope follower). The harness feeds no sensor/sound data to either side, so both engines see identical absent input — the all-black result is consistent with a sound-reactive pattern that has no signal to integrate, on BOTH sides.

dials.name: sliderIntegrationTime
dials.origEffect: No observable effect. --probe-controls reports maxDelta 0.00 / not responsive; confirmed by manual sweep at 0, 0.5 and 1 over 60 s / 5 fps windows each (300 frames per setting), all rendering exact black. meta.json confirms the value was actually applied (controlsApplied sliderIntegrationTime=[1]) with no warnings, so the dial was genuinely set. Effect unverifiable from output — almost certainly because the dial scales an audio integration window and there is no audio.
dials.portEffect: Identical: probe maxDelta 0.00 / not responsive, and the same manual 0 / 0.5 / 1 sweep over 60 s windows renders exact black, with the value confirmed applied. Effect unverifiable from output for the same reason.

feedback: Nothing actionable is visible from rendered output: the port matches the original exactly (bit-for-bit black) at every setting, window, seed and rig tested, so there is no divergence to fix from this evidence.

This pattern cannot be meaningfully verified by the current harness. Its output depends on sound/sensor globals that the harness never populates, so both engines correctly sit at zero and the comparison surface is empty. Re-verification needs a harness that injects a synthetic audio envelope (e.g. a driven level/peak signal with a known beat cadence) into both sides identically; only then can the integrator's attack/decay shape, the meaning of 'IntegrationTime', and the port's fidelity actually be judged.
The one thing that IS confirmed and worth keeping: the control surface is exactly right (single slider, matching name, kind and label), and the port has no compile or runtime error on our engine.
A future fixer should treat the score of 5 as 'unverified', not as 'partially wrong' — no defect was found, but near-zero behaviour was observable, so the port should not be assumed correct either.
